top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rewards three separable originating ideas: the tractable time-dependent pricing device, staggered contracts with the policy-rule framework, and the microfounded welfare-based synthesis. They are 25 to 45 years old and are the benchmark for monetary policy analysis, so maturity is not a concern. The estimation-side contributors (Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets) extended and quantified these ideas, so excluding them is a principled cut, though it is a real attribution cost. The post-2021 inflation, state-dependent pricing evidence and Phillips-curve fit limit what a citation can claim for the estimated descendants. They do not undo the originating ideas, so the citation should name the ideas and make no claim about forecasting performance. I rank P002 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) second because its credit boundary is cleaner, but its cross-country identification is weaker and it sits close to the 2024 institutions prize. P003 (Helpman, Melitz) is third. Its selection model is tested directly on firm-level data and has a clean two-name core, but credit for Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum falls outside it, its welfare results are sensitive to functional-form assumptions, and it follows the 2008 trade prize. Any of the three is preferable to no award. I rely on the supplied files and general knowledge and have not independently verified priority or adoption claims.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. Disclosed without adjudication: long committee overlap with Hassler, Krusell, Ellingsen and Svensson, and Chicago Booth adjunct and KVA Vice President roles. None of these involves a credited candidate in P001, P002 or P003. My corporate finance work is closest to B015 and B027, which are not in the proposal slate.
